audience.programmeDescription: Life Science and Technology is a joint bachelor at Delft and Leiden centred on living cells. It combines molecular biology and chemistry with mathematics, physics, biotechnology and laboratory work, including applications to health and sustainable production.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR option combines substantial molecular and biomedical science with laboratory practice and quantitative analysis. Shared rows show partial curricular relationships. UCR does not reproduce the specialist chemistry, biophysics and bioprocess-engineering sequence, the staged biotechnology practicals or the compulsory final research project.

curriculum.limitation: This shows the curriculum for students entering from 2025–2026 onward. The 30-EC minor remains open within approved options.

componentNotes.lst-y3-minor: 30 EC of minor study. Individually assembled or foreign course packages require approval and must not overlap with the compulsory curriculum.
componentNotes.lst-y3-bachelor-final-project: Compulsory 20-EC individual research project, including a thesis, supervised in an academic setting.
componentNotes.lst-y1-biotechnology-basic-techniques: Laboratory safety requirements apply. Its practical component precedes the later microbial-biotechnology practicum.

cellNotes.text: Includes microbial culture, bacterial transformation, protein production and purification, DNA analysis and basic bioinformatics. It is one broad laboratory course.
Digital image processing and computer vision; a biological or medical image project is not guaranteed.

concepts.label: Molecular life science, laboratory methods & quantitative analysis
concepts.concept: Molecular cell biology, biochemistry, practical laboratory methods, genetics, immunity, pharmacology and disease connect with research design, mathematics, programming and data/image analysis. The laboratory includes microbial culture, bacterial transformation, protein production and DNA methods. Life-cycle assessment and ethical reasoning support scientific responsibility. This related molecular-life-science programme does not reproduce the chemistry, biophysics, microbial/process-engineering sequence, multiple biotechnology practicums or compulsory 20-EC research project of Life Science and Technology.
